why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `enum ContextSource { Env, Launch }` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:105`), the `source` field on `Context`: which `init*` entry point produced it, for diagnostics and tests. No upstream counterpart — rclrs has one constructor family. (CORRECTED 2026-10-29 (phase-515 W0.c): a `Launch` variant, whose doc warned that it meant the launch-aware entry point was CALLED rather than that a launch file was parsed, left with the `init_with_launch*` entry points in issue 1931; the variants are `Env` and `Baked`.)

phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `enum ContextSource { Env, Launch, Baked }` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:157`) — `Baked` (`:173`) is the third variant, the one `Context::baked()` produces and `default_from_env()` / `from_env()` report on a freestanding build (`rust:ContextSource::Baked`). The enum compiles on every target now.

issue 1917 follow-up (2026-10-16) -- `Launch` DELETED. It recorded which entry point was called, and the caveat above is why that was worse than nothing: introspection said `Launch` for a context read from the environment, while the one entry that installs launch content reported `Env`/`Baked`. Two variants now, `Env` and `Baked`, each naming what was read.
